messages:
alex (PM): quick heads-up — BigCorp escalated their renewal. they want a formal 99.9% cross-region latency SLA for embeddings and an available dedicated pool by EOM. they flagged this as a blocker for renewal. asking product: do we re-prioritize or offer a temporary concession?

maria (CS): cc @alex (PM) they're pretty explicit: procurement + legal say SLA or they start a pilot with CompetitorX. revenue motion is ~$1.2M ARR.

li (Director): high level: big logo renewals weigh heavily but we can't keep changing roadmap for every ask. what are tradeoffs?

alex (PM): thinking RICE and sequencing. quick back-of-envelope: reach = 1 (one account), impact = 9 (revenue + ref), confidence = 6 (we can do it), effort = 40 dev-weeks -> very low RICE. but business impact might override raw score.

devin (Eng): technical note: cross-region SLA for embeddings implies multi-region KV cache and warm standby pools + active routing. not trivial. ballpark: 10-12 sprints to be safe. also need testing + infra cost.

sara (Data): also: quantization/ops changes for embeddings model for consistent p99 behavior. can mitigate with dedicated smaller model variant but quality risk.

maria (CS): options we've proposed: 1) short-term commercial SLA (non-binding, credit-based) + dedicated capacity pilot for 3 months; 2) full engineering push to deliver hard SLA; 3) migration help to cheaper tier (not ideal). they prefer #2 but might accept #1 if we give timeline.

alex (PM): proposal: offer #1 + clear launch criteria for #2. criteria: (a) validated canary in 2 regions with p99 < target on representative traffic; (b) infra autoscaling tested for spike X2; (c) legal-approved SLA template. If we hit criteria by EOM, commit to rollout.

li (Director): sounds reasonable. also create a prioritized RICE-lite doc that includes non-revenue multipliers (strategic weight for renewals). we use a multiplier when customer is >$500k ARR.

devin (Eng): can we do a scoped engineering patch: isolate embeddings to a single smaller model + dedicated pool to reduce variance? that could be 3 sprints and buys time.

maria (CS): customer would accept an interim dedicated pool if we promise a hardcut roadmap slot in Q2 for full distributed SLA. need sign-off from RevOps.

oncall-bot: deploy pipeline reported: no current deploys to prod clusters in progress.

alex (PM): action items: (1) @devin estimate scoped dedicated-pool MVP (3-4w) -> due 1719555700; (2) @sara quantify quality delta for smaller model -> due 1719555800; (3) @maria get written acceptance for interim SLA + RevOps approval -> due 1719555900; (4) @li confirm strategic multiplier policy -> due 1719555960. i'll draft a one-pager RICE-lite + stakeholder ask after those inputs.

li (Director): agree. also note: if any step reveals >30% quality regression we pause and escalate to exec.

maria (CS): I'll start the negotiation language: commercial credit + interim SLA + roadmap commitment. will loop in procurement. :thumbsup:

devin (Eng): I'll sketch the MVP infra diagram and perf knobs. low-level Qs later but timeline seems workable for an interim patch.

alex (PM): thanks all. keep updates in this thread so we have a single source of truth. if we end up committing more than 6 sprints we escalate to leadership.
